evidence.description: Starting another download cancels the existing task for the URL without waiting for it to finish.
Both completion paths remove the URL entry unconditionally, although that entry may already contain a replacement task.

candidates.explanation: Cancellation does not synchronously terminate a task. While the previous download is suspended, a replacement can be stored under the same URL. When the previous task resumes and handles cancellation, its cleanup removes the replacement's entry. The replacement can then continue without being tracked by activeTasks. Main-actor isolation does not prevent this interleaving across an await.
candidates.title: Obsolete tasks can remove replacement tasks from tracking

evidence.description: Cancel-all enumerates and cancels every task in the injected URLSession, not just tasks recorded by this loader.
URL-specific cancellation asynchronously searches session tasks by URL rather than preserving the identity of the task being canceled.

candidates.explanation: The cancellation methods act on the entire injected session after canceling their tracked tasks. Consequently, cancellation can affect other users of that session. The asynchronous enumeration also allows a newly started request to be canceled by an earlier cancellation call; matching only by URL does not distinguish the old request from its replacement.
candidates.title: Cancellation targets session tasks beyond the tracked operation

evidence.description: The response is discarded, and returned data is immediately wrapped, published, and cached without checking the HTTP status.

candidates.explanation: URLSession.data(from:) can return normally for HTTP error statuses. Because the response is ignored, an error response body can become a cached Item. Subsequent loads then reuse that body as though the image download succeeded.
candidates.title: HTTP error responses are published and cached as images

evidence.description: The catch block handles every thrown error solely by removing the task entry.

candidates.explanation: Non-cancellation failures receive the same silent handling as intentional cancellation. No failure is propagated, published, or recorded, so callers receive no indication that their requested download failed and the underlying cause is lost.
candidates.title: Download failures are silently discarded

evidence.description: The loader keeps downloaded items in an in-memory set.
Successful downloads add their items to the set.
Each cached item retains the complete downloaded Data.

candidates.explanation: The cache grows for every distinct successfully downloaded URL, and the class contains no removal or eviction path. Even cancellation leaves cached data intact. A long-lived loader therefore retains all downloaded payloads, allowing memory consumption to grow with its download history.
candidates.title: Downloaded image data is retained without an eviction path
